scope: passage-level projection of the Type-T minimum cubic multipole completion conflict catalog

claims.phase0_raw_c16_enumeration: left running as a diagnostic only; not used as a certificate
claims.phase1_passage_correspondence: PROVED (forward implications, at-most-one-supplier structurally verified over 238,269 supplier pairs on (4,55,7))
claims.phase2_c4_c8_passage_compilation: COMPUTATIONALLY_CERTIFIED for all three j=4 instances; cross-validated against the gadget-level catalog (2993/3000 sampled old clauses matched exactly, remaining 7/3000 were redundant/vacuous shared-vertex old clauses, not gaps) AND against a second, independently implemented general-m algorithm (type_t_port_c16_passage_hypergraph.py), which agrees exactly after a verification bug (see verification_bug_found_and_fixed) was fixed
claims.phase3_c16_passage_catalog: m=2 stage COMPUTATIONALLY_CERTIFIED for all three j=4 instances; for (4,55,7) the m=3, m=4 and m=5 layers are additionally compiled, so every admissible passage count (Phase 1 proves 2 <= m <= floor(16/3) = 5) now has a compiled layer. m=2/m=3/m=4 are complete outright: their lower shadow (all certified conflicts of support size < m) is itself complete, so no clause of that support size is missing. m=5 remains COMPLETE ONLY RELATIVE TO THE C8/m2/m3 LOWER SHADOW -- it was compiled before m=4 existed, so some of its 2,944,894 supports may be supersets of an m=4 conflict and would drop out on a rerun. Assembling the final minimal fixed-instance C16 CNF therefore still requires that one m=5 rerun; see c16_stages.remaining_work.
claims.phase4_m4_layer: COMPUTATIONALLY_CERTIFIED for (4,55,7): 3,971,519 verified minimal supports over all 87/87 canonical start vertices, no time budget, no truncation. Every support was individually reconstructed into a literal simple 16-cycle (0 rejected); an evenly spaced 2,000-support sample was additionally accepted by the structurally different generic materialize_passages + edge_path_cycle verifier (0 rejected); the lower-shadow pruning was audited by an unpruned re-run on start vertices 40-44 (368,081 raw supports, 55,337 surviving the domination filter, matching the pruned run exactly, symmetric difference 0); and the enumerator itself was cross-validated against the independently implemented general-m augmented-graph walk on 5 random passage subcatalogs (exact agreement on all 5). This is a completeness-and-soundness claim about the m=4 layer only. It is NOT an UNSAT result, NOT a counterexample, and NOT a claim that the assembled C16 formula has been tested.

verification_bug_found_and_fixed.description: verify_passage_conflicts originally materialized a full supplying triple/gadget (all its edges) rather than just the claimed passage; edge_path_cycle could then 'verify' a support via an unintended cycle through the supplier's other, unclaimed edges. Found because a second, independently implemented general-m search (type_t_port_c16_passage_hypergraph.py) disagreed with the m=2-specialized search (5007 vs 5052 on (4,55,7)). Fixed by materialize_passages in type_t_port_passages.py, which builds a minimal graph containing only the literally claimed passages. Both algorithms now agree exactly on all three instances.

multi_p3_redundancy_found_and_fixed.description: A completed graph selects exactly one linked-pair gadget ever, so it has exactly one joining edge and at most one p3-supplying structure physically present, and every candidate two-p3 support must be excluded. The original writeup mischaracterized ALL such candidates as merely 'sound but vacuous' after checking only vertex-disjointness; this was corrected after external review (see type_t_port_c16_passage_projection.md, 'second correction' section, and type_t_port_passages.drop_multi_p3_supports). The correct split, checked exhaustively against (4,55,7)'s 1,457 raw pre-fix C8 candidates: 331/1,457 are a same-gadget complementary pair (sides {a,b}/{c,d}), where forward channeling forces p3[a,c], p3[a,d], p3[b,c], p3[b,d] ALL true together the instant the gadget is selected -- a clause forbidding two of them is actively UNSOUND, not vacuous, since it could wrongly force UNSAT. The remaining candidates, from two different gadgets, are genuinely vacuous (exact-cover already forbids selecting two gadgets at once). Both cases have four fully distinct endpoint vertices, so vertex-disjointness alone cannot tell them apart. Either way the correct action is identical -- exclude the support -- and drop_multi_p3_supports plus the generator-level exclusions in enumerate_m2_passage_conflicts and enumerate_passage_conflicts already did that unconditionally for every two-p3 pair regardless of case, so no committed catalog was ever affected; only this writeup needed correcting.

c16_stages.method: type_t_port_c16_passage_general.py reuses the gadget-level general-m oracle-pruned search (type_t_port_c16_hypergraph.py) at the passage level, where per-vertex branching (~70 distinct passages) is far below the gadget-level figure (~1500) that search was built to cope with. Every m stage is pruned by lower-shadow domination against the already-compiled C8 catalog and every smaller already-verified C16 m stage. The specialized m=5 compiler exploits the (m,r,v) identity: either five p2 passages with core lengths {2,1,1,1,1}, or four p2 plus one p3 with five unit core lengths. Its exhaustive integer/bitmask DFS is independently checked support-by-support by a fixed-support alternating reconstruction, with an additional evenly spaced 2,000-support cross-check through the older generic materialize_passages + edge_path_cycle verifier. Because m=4 is not compiled yet, the committed m=5 summary is exact relative to the C8/m2/m3 lower shadow but may shrink after m=4 is added. The m=4 layer is compiled by the separate specialized compiler verifier/type_t_port_c16_passage_m4.py. m=4 is NOT a special case of the m=5 compiler: the (m,r,v) identity leaves core_total = 8 (b=0) or 7 (b=1) split into four positive parts, so bare-core segments of length up to 5 occur, whereas m=5 only ever needs lengths 1 and 2. The m=4 compiler therefore carries a precomputed table of every simple core path of length 1..5 (1,554 directed paths on this core) with each path's interior vertex bitmask, so whole-cycle simplicity is enforced with one integer AND per step.

m4.note: Compiled by verifier/type_t_port_c16_passage_m4.py. Unlike m=5 (core segments of length 1 or 2 only), m=4 admits bare-core segments of length up to 5, so the compiler carries a precomputed table of every simple core path of length 1..5 with its interior vertex bitmask. Per-support witnesses are intentionally omitted; the summary retains the exact count, canonical support-set commitment, verifier sample, and the two cross-validation reports.

m5.note: The 2,944,894 redundant per-support witnesses are intentionally omitted; the summary retains the exact count, canonical support-set commitment, verifier sample, and reproduction command. Rerun after m4 completion to remove m5 supports dominated by an m4 conflict.

c16_stages.note: raw_c16_diagnostic below (2,509,952 raw m=2 candidates before minimality/verification/lower-shadow pruning) predates this compilation and is retained only as a scale calibration point, not a partial certificate; the certified counts above are the real, independently verified figures.

remaining_work.task: rerun m=5 with the now-certified m=4 layer added to its lower shadow
remaining_work.why: Domination runs from smaller supports to larger ones. m=2/m=3/m=4 are unaffected by m=4's arrival (no size-4 set can dominate a size-2, -3 or -4 support), but a size-5 support that contains one of the 3,971,519 m=4 conflicts is subsumed and must not be emitted as a separate clause.
remaining_work.blocker: Not theory and not a missing technique -- purely artifact plumbing plus CPU. The committed m=4 summary is summary-only (count + SHA-256 commitment + samples), exactly as the m=5 summary is, so the 3,971,519 supports are not on disk to be loaded as a shadow; they must either be regenerated in-process (~260 s at 2 workers) or committed as a new ~30-80 MB binary artifact. The m=5 regeneration on top of that is roughly 900 CPU-seconds. Neither step needs new mathematics.

raw_c16_diagnostic.note: m=2 alone already exceeds the entire gadget-level C8 raw count; m=3,4,5 not awaited. Retained as a scale calibration point for the passage-level C16 attempt, not as a partial certificate.

verification.method: C4/C8/m2/m3 emitted supports are independently re-verified by materializing a MINIMAL graph containing exactly the claimed passages (materialize_passages) and locating the literal cycle via edge_path_cycle. The 2,944,894-support m5 layer is exhaustively verified by a separate fixed-support alternating reconstruction and simple literal-witness check; an evenly spaced 2,000-support sample is additionally accepted by the older materialize_passages + edge_path_cycle implementation. The 3,971,519-support m4 layer is verified the same way as m5 (exhaustive support-local alternating reconstruction to a literal simple 16-cycle, plus a 2,000-support sample through the generic verifier). Note the generic verifier is the weaker of the two: it accepts whenever SOME 16-cycle exists in the minimal materialization, not necessarily one using all four claimed passages. For these supports the two coincide, because the shadow they survived (complete C8 + complete C16 m=2 + complete C16 m=3) already contains every conflict of support size 2 and 3, and type_t_port_core_dyadic_avoidance.md rules out a bare-core 16-cycle -- so any 16-cycle in the materialization must use all four passages. The support-local verifier is what actually certifies that, for every support and not just the sample.
verification.cross_check_vs_gadget_catalog: 3000-clause random sample of the prior gadget-level (4,55,7) C8 catalog checked against the new passage catalog; 2993/3000 exact matches, 7/3000 explained as redundant old clauses whose two identities already shared a vertex (structurally excluded by exact-cover, not a missing conflict)
verification.cross_check_vs_second_algorithm: type_t_port_c16_passage_hypergraph.py's general-m augmented-graph walk reproduces the m=2-specialized algorithm's C8 result exactly (5007/5044/6359) on all three j=4 instances
verification.cross_check_m4_vs_second_algorithm: type_t_port_c16_passage_hypergraph.py's general-m augmented-graph walk cannot run at max_m=4 on the full 1,302-passage catalog, but restricting the passage catalog leaves the bare core untouched, so both searches must agree exactly on any subset. 5 random subcatalog trials (40 passages each) agree exactly with the m=4 compiler, symmetric difference 0 on every trial.
verification.cross_check_m4_lower_shadow_pruning: Start vertices 40-44 re-enumerated with shadow pruning disabled: 368,081 raw size-4 supports, of which 55,337 survive an independent post-hoc domination filter -- exactly the 55,337 the pruned run emits for those starts, with 0 supports on either side of the symmetric difference.

status_note: Every admissible m layer for (4,55,7) is now compiled (m=2,3,4 outright; m=5 relative to the pre-m4 shadow). The manifest deliberately stays BOUNDED_INCOMPLETE: the final minimal C16 CNF has not been assembled, the m=5 rerun against the m=4 shadow has not been done, and no SAT test of the fixed completion instance has been run. No UNSAT certificate and no counterexample is claimed.
